name: De Facto World Map
description: Who actually controls territory, rather than who claims it, as of 2026-10. By Trevor Christensen, https://trevorc.com/projects/de-facto-world-map. Map data ODbL 1.0: borders © OpenStreetMap contributors (via Overture Maps), with Natural Earth and geoBoundaries; Antarctic stations from COMNAP, non-commercial use.

properties.name: Dhekelia Cantonment
properties.note: A UK Sovereign Base Area retained when Cyprus became independent in 1960.

properties.name: Guantanamo Bay Naval Base
properties.note: Leased to the United States since 1903; Cuba considers the lease invalid.

properties.name: Brazilian Island
properties.note: A river island claimed by both Brazil and Uruguay.

properties.name: United Nations Buffer Zone in Cyprus
properties.note: The UN buffer zone (Green Line) between the Republic of Cyprus and Northern Cyprus, patrolled by UNFICYP since 1974.

properties.name: Siachen Glacier
properties.note: Held by India since 1984; claimed by Pakistan.

properties.name: Baikonur
properties.note: Leased to Russia by Kazakhstan for the Baikonur Cosmodrome; administered by Russia until 2050.

properties.name: Akrotiri Sovereign Base Area
properties.note: A UK Sovereign Base Area retained when Cyprus became independent in 1960.

properties.name: Southern Patagonian Ice Field
properties.note: A stretch of the Chile-Argentina border that has never been demarcated.

properties.name: Wake Island
properties.note: Individual reefs and islands are occupied by China, Vietnam, the Philippines, Malaysia, and Taiwan.

properties.name: Bajo Nuevo Bank
properties.note: Awarded to Colombia by the International Court of Justice in 2012.

properties.name: Serranilla Bank
properties.note: Awarded to Colombia by the International Court of Justice in 2012.

properties.name: Scarborough Shoal
properties.note: Controlled by Chinese coast guard ships since a 2012 standoff; claimed by the Philippines.

properties.name: Abkhazia
properties.note: Self-governing since the 1992-93 war, with a permanent Russian military presence.

properties.name: South Ossetia
properties.note: Self-governing since the early 1990s; Russian forces have been based there since the 2008 war.

properties.name: Transnistria
properties.note: Self-governing since the 1992 war, with a Russian garrison.

properties.name: Russian-occupied Ukraine
properties.note: Crimea (occupied since 2014) and the parts of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson, Kharkiv and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts held since 2022: about a fifth of Ukraine. Russia claims to have annexed Crimea and four oblasts. Drawn as the Ukrainian municipalities (OpenStreetMap level 3, via geoBoundaries) that are mostly occupied on DeepStateMap's map, so the line is approximate at the scale of individual municipalities.

properties.name: Gray zone along the front
properties.note: Municipalities mostly in the zone DeepStateMap marks as unknown status, where neither side has established control. No ceasefire was in force in October 2026; this is ground where infiltration and drones keep either side from establishing control.

properties.name: West Bank and East Jerusalem
properties.note: Under Israeli military occupation since 1967; East Jerusalem was annexed by Israel. The Palestinian Authority administers civil affairs in Areas A and B (about 40% of the West Bank).

properties.name: Israeli-held Gaza
properties.note: East of the 'yellow line' set by the October 2025 ceasefire, which Israel has since pushed westward. Israel holds about 63 to 65% of the Strip (64.9% by the UN's count in June 2026, about 63% by Israeli estimates in October) and says it will stay until Hamas disarms. The Strip's outline follows OpenStreetMap.

properties.name: Hamas-held Gaza
properties.note: West of the yellow line: Gaza City west of Salah al-Din Street, Nuseirat, Deir al-Balah, western Khan Younis and al-Mawasi, about 36% of the Strip. Israel has moved the line west repeatedly since the October 2025 ceasefire. Traced from landmarks in news reports, so expect errors of up to a kilometer.

properties.name: Philadelphi corridor
properties.note: The strip along Gaza's border with Egypt, held by Israel since May 2024, which separates Hamas-held Gaza from Egypt all the way to the sea. Drawn 400 m wide along OpenStreetMap's border line.

properties.name: Golan Heights
properties.note: Held by Israel since 1967 and annexed in 1981; the United States recognized the annexation in 2019, but nearly all other states consider it occupied Syrian territory. Includes the Shebaa Farms, claimed by Lebanon.

properties.name: Southern Lebanon
properties.note: Israel has occupied a strip of southern Lebanon since its March 2026 invasion, behind a 'yellow line' about 5 to 15 km deep that includes Khiam and Beaufort Castle, and says it will stay until northern Israel is secure. Traced from the Guardian's 31 May 2026 map; Israel put the area at about 600 km² in August.

properties.name: Syrian buffer zone and Mount Hermon
properties.note: Israeli forces have held the 1974 buffer zone and the Syrian summit of Mount Hermon since December 2024, plus a few positions just beyond it, about 350 km² in all (drawn as the zone plus a 1.5 km margin). US-mediated security talks in 2026 have produced no withdrawal.

properties.name: Suwayda
properties.note: Run since July 2025 by Druze factions under Sheikh Hikmat al-Hijri's National Guard and, since April 2026, his self-declared Jabal Bashan administration. The government holds only villages on the western edge and the eastern desert.

properties.name: Houthi-held Yemen
properties.note: The north and west, home to most of Yemen's population. A Houthi offensive from 3 September 2026 took the Red Sea coast from Hays and al-Khawkhah to Mokha and Dhubab, briefly giving them the whole Yemeni shore of Bab al-Mandab, then cut Taiz city's last road out. A Saudi-backed counteroffensive retook the strait itself on 5 October. The south is held by government and Saudi-backed forces; the separatist STC lost its territory in January 2026.

properties.name: Yemeni front line
properties.note: Districts fought over in October 2026: Dhubab, where government forces hold the strait and airport and the Houthis the north; the mountains west and south of Taiz city, which the Houthis have encircled; the Marib fronts at Madghal and Raghwan; Qa'tabah in al-Dhale; and the populated western edge of Khab wa Ash Sha'f in al-Jawf, split here by eye. Nearly every battlefield claim comes from one side.

properties.name: Eastern and southern Libya
properties.note: Held by Khalifa Haftar's Libyan National Army and the parallel eastern government, including Sirte, Jufra and the Fezzan; the lines have not moved since the 2020 ceasefire. Rivalry in Tripoli is among the western factions, not with Haftar.

properties.name: RSF-held Sudan
properties.note: Almost all of Darfur, where El Fasher fell in October 2025, and all of West Kordofan, where Babanusa's army base fell in December 2025. The RSF also holds ground west and south of El Obeid. Governed by the RSF-led Tasis parallel government.

properties.name: Dar Zaghawa
properties.note: Dar Zaghawa near the Chad border, where the RSF and the army-allied Darfur Joint Forces have traded towns through 2026; the RSF took Kernoi in March and Um Baru around July. At Tina remains with the Joint Forces.

properties.name: Jebel Marra and Tawila
properties.note: The SLM faction of Abdel Wahid al-Nur holds parts of these localities, outside both army and RSF control.

properties.name: Nuba Mountains and southern Blue Nile
properties.note: SPLM-North (al-Hilu) has held the core of the Nuba Mountains since 2011. With the RSF it took Kurmuk and Geisan in southern Blue Nile in 2026. Kadugli and Dilling remain army-held, and Kadugli has been besieged again since March 2026.

properties.name: North Kordofan front
properties.note: The army retook Bara in July 2026, Sodari town on 25 September and al-Mazroub on 2 October. The RSF still holds Um Badr and Hamrat al-Sheikh in the west of Sodari locality, and El Obeid is close to besieged.

properties.name: Abyei
properties.note: Claimed by both Sudan and South Sudan and patrolled by UN peacekeepers (UNISFA), whose mandate runs to 15 November 2026. South Sudanese forces and RSF checkpoints operate there despite its demilitarized status.

properties.name: AFC/M23-held Kivu
properties.note: Held by AFC/M23, backed by Rwanda, since the capture of Goma (January 2025) and Bukavu (February 2025). Southern Masisi and western Kalehe change hands almost weekly, and Rwanda missed a July 2026 deadline to withdraw its troops.

properties.name: Walikale, Lubero and Mwenga
properties.note: Front-line territories where AFC/M23 holds the eastern or southern parts and the army and Wazalendo militias hold the rest. M23 briefly took Uvira in December 2025, but it returned to the army in January 2026.

properties.name: Puntland
properties.note: Has governed itself without recognizing the federal government since 2024, and in August 2026 its forces seized federally aligned bases in Galkayo and Bosaso. It is also fighting Islamic State in the Cal Miskaad mountains. Its edges with Somaliland and SSC-Khatumo are disputed.

properties.name: North Eastern State (SSC-Khatumo)
properties.note: Taken from Somaliland by SSC-Khatumo forces in 2023 and recognized by Mogadishu in 2025 as the North Eastern State, a federal member state aligned with the federal government. Somaliland still claims it, and Puntland disputes parts of Sool and Sanaag.

properties.name: Jubaland
properties.note: Has rejected the federal government's authority since November 2024 and in December 2025 amended its constitution to call itself a government rather than a federal member state. Holds Kismayo, the Lower Juba border towns, and Doolow and (since August 2026) Beled Hawo in Gedo; federal forces hold Garbahaarey and Luuq. Al-Shabaab holds much of the Lower Juba countryside.

properties.name: Bardhere and El Wak
properties.note: Gedo districts disputed between Jubaland and federal forces since late 2024; Jubaland retook Bardhere in February 2025, and the towns have changed hands since.

properties.name: al-Shabaab-held south
properties.note: Al-Shabaab has held the Juba valley throughout its existence; its 2025 offensive retook towns lost in 2022-23 in Middle Shabelle, Hiiraan and Galgaduud, and it took Teedan in Hiiraan in August 2026. Drawn where it holds the district seat; it also controls much of the countryside around government towns (see the presence layer).

properties.name: Rakhine and Paletwa
properties.note: The Arakan Army holds 14 of Rakhine's 17 townships plus Paletwa in Chin State; the junta keeps Sittwe, Kyaukphyu and Manaung, and its September 2026 counteroffensive made little headway.

properties.name: Wa State
properties.note: The northern Wa region (the Wa Self-Administered Division). The UWSA also holds a separate southern area along the Thai border, not drawn here.

properties.name: Mongla
properties.note: Special Region 4, self-administered under a ceasefire since 1989.

properties.name: Kokang and Kutkai
properties.note: Held by the MNDAA since Operation 1027 in 2023-24, plus Kutkai, taken from its former ally the TNLA in March 2026. It returned Lashio to the junta in April 2025 under Chinese pressure.

properties.name: Ta'ang areas
properties.note: The Palaung Self-Administered Zone plus Namhkam and Namtu. Under a China-brokered ceasefire the TNLA handed Mogok and Momeik back in late 2025, and the junta has demanded Namhkam and Namtu as well.

properties.name: KIA-held Kachin
properties.note: Townships the Kachin Independence Army holds outright, along the Chinese border and north of Myitkyina. It holds most of the rest of rural Kachin State too (see the presence layer); the junta holds Myitkyina, Bhamo town and Putao.

properties.name: Taiwan
properties.note: Claimed by the People's Republic of China, which has never governed it.

properties.name: Kosovo
properties.note: Claimed by Serbia since Kosovo declared independence in 2008.

properties.name: Somaliland
properties.note: Claimed by Somalia.

properties.name: Northern Cyprus
properties.note: Claimed by the Republic of Cyprus.

properties.name: Abkhazia
properties.note: Claimed by Georgia.

properties.name: South Ossetia
properties.note: Claimed by Georgia.

properties.name: Transnistria
properties.note: Claimed by Moldova.

properties.name: Crimea
properties.note: Claimed by Ukraine; occupied and annexed by Russia in 2014.

properties.name: Sahrawi Free Zone
properties.note: Claimed by Morocco as part of its southern provinces.

properties.name: Western Sahara (Moroccan-held)
properties.note: Claimed by the Sahrawi Republic; held by Morocco west of the berm.

properties.name: Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan
properties.note: Held by Pakistan; claimed by India.

properties.name: Aksai Chin and Shaksgam
properties.note: Held by China; claimed by India.

properties.name: Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh
properties.note: Held by India; claimed by Pakistan.

properties.name: Siachen Glacier
properties.note: Held by India since 1984; claimed by Pakistan.

properties.name: Arunachal Pradesh and other areas
properties.note: Held by India; claimed by China.

properties.name: Northern Bhutan
properties.note: Held by Bhutan; claimed by China.

properties.name: Kalapani
properties.note: Held by India; claimed by Nepal.

properties.name: Golan Heights
properties.note: Held by Israel since 1967; claimed by Syria.

properties.name: Southern Lebanon
properties.note: Lebanese territory occupied by Israel since March 2026.

properties.name: Shebaa Farms
properties.note: Held by Israel; claimed by Lebanon.

properties.name: East Jerusalem
properties.note: Held and annexed by Israel; claimed by Palestine.

properties.name: Southern Kuril Islands
properties.note: Held by Russia since 1945; claimed by Japan as its Northern Territories.

properties.name: Falkland Islands
properties.note: Held by the United Kingdom; claimed by Argentina.

properties.name: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
properties.note: Held by the United Kingdom; claimed by Argentina.

properties.name: Guayana Esequiba
properties.note: Held by Guyana; claimed by Venezuela, which declared it a Venezuelan state in 2024.

properties.name: Gibraltar
properties.note: Held by the United Kingdom; claimed by Spain.

properties.name: Ceuta, Melilla, and Spanish islets
properties.note: Held by Spain; claimed by Morocco.

properties.name: Paracel Islands
properties.note: Held by China since 1974; claimed by Vietnam.

properties.name: Paracel Islands
properties.note: Held by China; claimed by Taiwan.

properties.name: Spratly Islands
properties.note: Occupied in parts by five claimants; China claims them all.

properties.name: Spratly Islands
properties.note: Occupied in parts by five claimants; Vietnam claims them all.

properties.name: Spratly Islands
properties.note: Occupied in parts by five claimants; the Philippines claims part of them.

properties.name: Spratly Islands
properties.note: Occupied in parts by five claimants; Taiwan claims them all.

properties.name: Scarborough Shoal
properties.note: Controlled by Chinese coast guard ships since 2012; claimed by the Philippines.

properties.name: Senkaku Islands
properties.note: Held by Japan; claimed by China as the Diaoyu Islands.

properties.name: Senkaku Islands
properties.note: Held by Japan; claimed by Taiwan.

properties.name: Liancourt Rocks
properties.note: Held by South Korea as Dokdo; claimed by Japan as Takeshima.

properties.name: Abu Musa and the Tunbs
properties.note: Held by Iran since 1971; claimed by the UAE.

properties.name: Hala'ib Triangle
properties.note: Held by Egypt; claimed by Sudan.

properties.name: Ilemi Triangle
properties.note: Administered by Kenya; claimed by South Sudan.

properties.name: Kafia Kingi
properties.note: Held by Sudan; claimed by South Sudan.

properties.name: Southern Belize
properties.note: Held by Belize; claimed by Guatemala, pending at the International Court of Justice.

properties.name: Guantánamo Bay
properties.note: Leased to the United States since 1903; Cuba considers the lease invalid.

properties.name: Mayotte
properties.note: Held by France; claimed by Comoros.

properties.name: Scattered Islands
properties.note: Held by France; claimed by Madagascar.

properties.name: Tromelin Island
properties.note: Held by France; claimed by Mauritius.

properties.name: Tigri Area
properties.note: Held by Guyana; claimed by Suriname.

properties.name: Lawa Headwaters
properties.note: Held by France (French Guiana); claimed by Suriname.

properties.name: Olivenza
properties.note: Held by Spain; claimed by Portugal.

properties.name: Matthew and Hunter Islands
properties.note: Held by France (New Caledonia); claimed by Vanuatu.

properties.name: Wake Island
properties.note: Held by the United States; claimed by the Marshall Islands.

properties.name: Navassa Island
properties.note: Held by the United States; claimed by Haiti.

properties.name: Corner of Artigas
properties.note: Held by Brazil; claimed by Uruguay.

properties.name: Doumeira Islands
properties.note: Held by Eritrea; claimed by Djibouti.

properties.name: North Korea
properties.note: South Korea's constitution claims the whole peninsula. North Korea no longer claims the South: its March 2026 constitutional revision dropped reunification and bounded its territory by the Republic of Korea to the south, though it leaves the sea border undefined.

properties.name: Russian-occupied Ukraine
properties.note: Ukraine's internationally recognized territory.

properties.name: Rest of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson
properties.note: Russia claims to have annexed these four oblasts in full in September 2022, including the parts it has never held, among them the cities of Zaporizhzhia and Kherson.

properties.name: West Bank and Gaza
properties.note: The territory of the State of Palestine as recognized by most UN members.

properties.name: Sool and Buhodle
properties.note: Claimed by Somaliland, which lost Las Anod to SSC-Khatumo forces in 2023.

properties.name: Brazilian Antarctica (unofficial)
properties.note: Unofficial zone of interest, not a formal claim.

properties.name: Argentine Antarctica
properties.note: Claim held in abeyance by the Antarctic Treaty (1959).

properties.name: Australian Antarctic Territory
properties.note: Claim held in abeyance by the Antarctic Treaty (1959).

properties.name: Ross Dependency
properties.note: Claim held in abeyance by the Antarctic Treaty (1959).

properties.name: Antárctica
properties.note: Claim held in abeyance by the Antarctic Treaty (1959).

properties.name: Queen Maud Land
properties.note: Claim held in abeyance by the Antarctic Treaty (1959). Southern boundary of Norwegian claim is undefined.

properties.name: Adélie Land
properties.note: Claim held in abeyance by the Antarctic Treaty (1959).

properties.name: British Antarctic Territory
properties.note: Claim held in abeyance by the Antarctic Treaty (1959).

properties.name: Peter I Island
properties.note: Claim held in abeyance by the Antarctic Treaty (1959).

properties.name: Southern and central Somalia
properties.note: Holds or contests most of the countryside of southern and central Somalia, about 30% of the country's land, and taxes trade in government towns; it besieges El Dhere and stepped up attacks around Mogadishu in mid-2026.

properties.name: Kachin State
properties.note: The KIA holds most of rural Kachin State and contests Bhamo; the junta holds Myitkyina, Bhamo town and Putao.

properties.name: Chin State
properties.note: Chin resistance forces hold most of the countryside and the southern towns; the junta retook Falam and Tonzang in 2026 and holds Hakha.

properties.name: Sagaing and Magway
properties.note: People's Defense Forces contest much of the dry zone, but the junta has retaken several Sagaing towns since the 2025-26 election and put dozens of townships under martial law.

properties.name: Karenni (Kayah) State
properties.note: Karenni resistance forces hold much of the state, though the junta has retaken some towns since 2025.

properties.name: Karen (Kayin) State
properties.note: The KNU and allied forces control large rural areas along the Thai border.

properties.name: Central and western Mali
properties.note: JNIM rules much of the countryside through taxes and local deals, and since April 2026 has besieged Bamako, which is resupplied by army-escorted fuel convoys. It does not hold major towns.

properties.name: Northern and eastern Burkina Faso
properties.note: JNIM operates across roughly half of Burkina Faso, blockading many towns that the junta nominally holds.

properties.name: Ménaka, Gao, Tillabéri and Tahoua
properties.note: Islamic State Sahel dominates the Ménaka region and the borderlands of western Niger.

properties.name: Kidal region
properties.note: Tuareg separatists and JNIM took Kidal, Tessalit and Aguelhok in April 2026, but the army and Russian forces retook Kidal unopposed on 6 October. The FLA remains around Tessalit and Tinzaouatene near the Algerian border.

properties.name: Lake Chad and northern Borno
properties.note: ISWAP holds the Lake Chad islands and much of northern Borno's countryside.

properties.name: Sambisa and the Mandara Mountains
properties.note: Boko Haram's JAS faction operates from the Sambisa forest and the Mandara Mountains.

properties.name: Amhara
properties.note: Fano militias have fought the federal government since 2023 and hold much of rural Amhara.

properties.name: Cabo Delgado
properties.note: Islamic State Mozambique remains active despite Rwandan and Mozambican operations.

properties.name: Northwest and Southwest Cameroon
properties.note: Anglophone separatists have fought for an independent 'Ambazonia' since 2017.

properties.name: Former tribal areas
properties.note: The Pakistani Taliban has resurged in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's former tribal districts since 2021.

properties.name: Balochistan
properties.note: Baloch separatists stage frequent attacks across the province, including the 2025 Jaffar Express hijacking.

properties.name: Catatumbo and Arauca
properties.note: The ELN has dominated these border departments since its 2025 Catatumbo offensive.

properties.name: Cauca and Guaviare
properties.note: FARC dissident factions control rural areas and coca routes.

properties.name: Ouest and Artibonite
properties.note: The Viv Ansanm gang coalition controls most of Port-au-Prince and much of the Artibonite valley.

properties.name: Upper Nile and Jonglei
properties.note: Fighting resumed in 2025 after Riek Machar's arrest; opposition forces hold Akobo County and much of rural Lou Nuer Jonglei and Upper Nile, while the army holds Nasir, Ulang and the state capitals.

properties.name: Beni, Lubero and Ituri
properties.note: The Islamic State-affiliated ADF carries out frequent massacres of civilians.
